stories.headline: Tencent launches Hy4 with vision and computer use, says weights will follow; trails closed models

key_facts.fact: Tencent released Hy4 on November 4, saying it places its Hy line among the strongest open-source models for the first time.
key_facts.excerpt: Today, we're releasing Hy4, another major leap forward that places Hy among the strongest open-source models for the first time.

key_facts.fact: Hy4 supports vision perception and computer use for the first time, working across command-line and graphical interfaces, with targeted training on software such as Blender and CAD.
key_facts.excerpt: Hy4 also supports computer use for the first time, working across command-line interfaces (CLI) and graphical user interfaces (GUI). Through targeted training on specialized software such as Blender and CAD...

key_facts.fact: The weights are not out yet: Tencent says it plans to release weights and system cards in the coming days, with a focus on cybersecurity and biological safety.
key_facts.excerpt: Tencent Hy plans to release model weights and system cards in the coming days, reinforcing its commitment to responsible open-source AI development, with a focus on cybersecurity and biological safety.

key_facts.fact: In a blind evaluation run with Tencent's own fintech unit, using 213 finance professionals and 579 real tasks, Hy4 scored 3.04, against 2.97 for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 and 2.68 each for Kimi K3.1 Pro and GLM-5.3.
key_facts.excerpt: Evaluation scores: Hy4 (3.04), DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 (2.97), Kimi K3.1 Pro (2.68), and GLM-5.3 (2.68).

key_facts.fact: Tencent concedes a notable gap to top proprietary models on research-level math, long-horizon coding, model self-improvement and advanced visual question answering.
key_facts.excerpt: a notable gap remains between it and top proprietary models, particularly on challenging internal benchmarks for research-level mathematics, long-horizon coding, model self-improvement, and advanced visual question answering.

key_facts.fact: On Tencent's own benchmark chart, Hy4 scores 44.4 on Terminal Bench 4.0, against 66.4 for Claude Opus 5.5 and 55.5 for GPT-6.1 Sol; on OSWorld 2.1, a computer-use test, it scores 78.9 against 81.8 and 75.2.
key_facts.excerpt: On Terminal Bench 4.0, Hy4 scores 44.4, against 66.4 for Claude Opus 5.5 and 55.5 for GPT-6.1 Sol... OSWorld 2.1, a test of operating a computer, where it scores 78.9 to Claude's 81.8, ahead of GPT-6.1 Sol's 75.2. All the figures are Tencent's

key_facts.fact: Tencent says Hy4, paired with its Hyra 2.0 harness, optimized internal pre-training infrastructure and autonomously trained a smaller-model variant that beat the official baseline, and that it will open-source two foundation models co-developed this way, HyCell and HyPDE.
key_facts.excerpt: We are also laying the groundwork for recursive self-improvement... Hy4 optimized our internal pre-training infrastructure for smaller models with the same architecture, and autonomously trained a variant that outperforms the official Jev baseline... we are open-sourcing two foundation models co-developed by Hy4 and Hyra 2.0: HyCell... and HyPDE

key_facts.fact: Pricing is unchanged from the preview at about $0.90 per million input tokens and $2.70 per million output tokens, with 50% off on Tencent Cloud TokenHub through December 31.
key_facts.excerpt: approximately US$0.90 per million input tokens, US$2.70 per million output tokens... Hy4 will be available on Tencent Cloud TokenHub at 50% off its standard pricing, with this offer running through December 31, 2026.

stories.headline: Exit poll: 56% of voters call AI and data centers a major factor as Democrats win Congress

key_facts.fact: In the NBC News exit poll, 56% of voters called AI and data centers a crucial (23%) or major (33%) factor in their congressional vote, in an election that gave Democrats control of the House and Senate.
key_facts.excerpt: 56% of voters called artificial intelligence and data centers a crucial or major factor in their vote for Congress... 23% called AI and data centers crucial and 33% called them a major factor.

key_facts.fact: Voters in that group backed Democrats 64% to 34%; those calling the issue minor or no factor backed Republicans 57% to 41%. The poll shows an association, not proof that the issue decided their vote.
key_facts.excerpt: Voters in the crucial-or-major group supported Democratic congressional candidates by 64% to 34%... 57% backed Republicans and 41% backed Democrats. Those are associations within the survey

key_facts.fact: AI and data centers still ranked last of the five issues tested, behind government corruption (90%), cost of living (89%), the war in Iran (74%) and immigration enforcement (73%).
key_facts.excerpt: That put the issue at the bottom of the five topics surveyed. Government corruption led at 90 percent, followed by cost of living at 89 percent, the war in Iran at 74 percent, and immigration enforcement at 73 percent.

key_facts.fact: 57% said AI will do more to hurt society and 24% more to help; asked which party would handle AI better, 29% chose Democrats, 27% Republicans and 43% neither. 76% opposed a new data center in their own community.
key_facts.excerpt: Fifty-seven percent said AI would do more to hurt society, compared with 24%... 29% chose Democrats, 27% chose Republicans and 43% said neither party... Seventy-six percent opposed a new facility in their community

key_facts.fact: Voters in at least 29 US jurisdictions passed data center bans or restrictions on Tuesday, November 3, according to The Washington Post.
key_facts.excerpt: Voters in at least 29 jurisdictions across the country passed bans or restrictions on data centers Tuesday

key_facts.fact: Politico reports the result as a warning to politicians aligned with the AI industry, after Silicon Valley donors spent hundreds of millions of dollars over the cycle to boost pro-industry Republicans.
key_facts.excerpt: Democrats' decisive midterms victory marked a warning shot to politicians who choose to align with the artificial intelligence industry... Silicon Valley's biggest donors who over the cycle poured hundreds of millions of dollars to boost pro-industry Republicans

stories.headline: Google turns off AI by default for K-12 students; schools rejecting AI lose Search too

key_facts.fact: Google announced on November 3 that Gemini, Gemini Notebook, Gemini in Classroom and Google Search will be off for K-12 student accounts until administrators explicitly turn them on, reversing an August change that enabled AI by default.
key_facts.excerpt: Access to these products will be entirely off for K-12 student accounts until school administrators explicitly turn them on... In August, Google enabled certain AI features by default in the Classroom learning platform.

key_facts.fact: Google education chief Chris Phillips told The New York Times that schools banning AI entirely will lose Search, because the two are deeply integrated.
key_facts.excerpt: "Search and A.I. are deeply integrated," said Chris Phillips... If a school has banned A.I., he added, students "will not have access to search, and they'll see a message from their school that indicates it's not available."

key_facts.fact: After the backlash, Google said schools can enable Gemini, Gemini Notebook and Search individually, and that AI Mode and AI Overviews will offer step-by-step guided learning in school Search.
key_facts.excerpt: Schools are in control: They can choose to turn ON one, two, or all of these services individually... AI Mode and AI Overviews will offer step-by-step guided learning through problems

key_facts.fact: The clarification does not provide Search without AI: NBC News reports that schools still cannot use Search without AI features such as AI-generated summaries.
key_facts.excerpt: But schools would still not be able to use Search without certain AI features like AI-generated summaries, given AI's growing integration into the company's search functionality.

key_facts.fact: Sen. Bernie Sanders called the policy "extortion" and New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani said Google is using monopoly power to force AI into public schools.
key_facts.excerpt: "Google is trying to use its monopoly power to force AI into our public schools," Mamdani wrote on X. Sanders wrote that "Google is threatening schools," referring to the policy as "extortion."

key_facts.fact: American Federation of Teachers president Randi Weingarten said Google "has prioritized its business interests over the education of our children."
key_facts.excerpt: "It is unfortunate that Google has prioritized its business interests over the education of our children," said Randi Weingarten, president of the American Federation of Teachers

key_facts.fact: Google will test Guided Learning in Search in select US schools starting this month before a broader expansion; teachers will be able to see transcripts of chatbot interactions on student accounts in the school version.
key_facts.excerpt: The company will test this approach in select schools in the US starting this month before a broader expansion. In the school version of Guided Learning, teachers will be able to access transcripts of chatbot interactions on student accounts.

stories.headline: Apple opens Siri AI to all developers in iOS 27.3 beta, and also tests Apple Intelligence in China

key_facts.fact: Starting November 3, a Developer Preview in the iOS, iPadOS, macOS and visionOS 27.3 betas lets any developer bring app content and actions into Siri AI through App Intents.
key_facts.excerpt: Starting today with the iOS 27.3, iPadOS 27.3, macOS 27.3, and visionOS 27.3 betas, a new Developer Preview enables any developer to integrate their app with Siri AI

key_facts.fact: Apple is adding "skills" that teach Siri AI to combine several actions, and Siri AI can now surface any entity in the Spotlight semantic index rather than only those fitting an existing schema.
key_facts.excerpt: we're also introducing skills to let you teach Siri AI how to combine several actions into a single experience. And Siri AI can now surface any entity in the Spotlight semantic index, not just the ones that fit an existing schema.

key_facts.fact: The integrations reach customers in a few months, with App Store submission opening in the spring; Apple says terms and usage policies will follow.
key_facts.excerpt: This preview provides early access before first shipping to customers in a few months; and with submission to the App Store opening up in the spring... we will follow up with more details about the terms and usage policies

key_facts.fact: Siri AI remains unavailable in the EU on iOS, iPadOS and watchOS, and server-based features have daily limits, with expanded access to come for a fee.
key_facts.excerpt: Siri AI is currently unavailable in the EU in iOS, iPadOS, and watchOS... Expanded access to such features will be available for a fee in the future.

key_facts.fact: The same beta makes select Apple Intelligence features testable in China for the first time, with Siri, Writing Tools and Visual Intelligence integrating Alibaba's Qwen; Siri AI itself is excluded.
key_facts.excerpt: Select Apple Intelligence features are now available in China, with Apple testing the functionality in the iOS 27.3 beta... integrate Alibaba's Qwen model... Apple Intelligence in China does not include Siri AI

key_facts.fact: Apple's public launch in China is slated for December with iOS 27.3; the plan was announced on October 30, and the beta went live on November 3.
key_facts.excerpt: Apple is launching an iOS 27.3 beta next week that will bring some of the initial Apple Intelligence features to the Chinese market... with a full iOS 27.3 release scheduled for December.

stories.headline: AI inference startup Fal raises $1.3B led by Bessemer at $16B, double its April valuation

key_facts.fact: Fal, which hosts and runs AI video, image and audio models, raised a $1.3 billion Series F led by Bessemer Venture Partners, with Nvidia, Sound Ventures, HOF Capital and T. Rowe Price participating.
key_facts.excerpt: Bessemer Venture Partners led the Series F round... Nvidia Corp., Sound Ventures, HOF Capital and T. Rowe Price Group Inc. also participated.

key_facts.fact: The deal values Fal at $16 billion, double its $8 billion valuation in April, Bloomberg reported.
key_facts.excerpt: The deal values Fal at $16 billion, double its $8 billion valuation in April, Bloomberg reported.

key_facts.fact: Fal announced the Series F together with the $350 million Series E that Sequoia led in April, for $1.65 billion combined; investors have now put more than $1.9 billion into the company.
key_facts.excerpt: That Series E round raised $350 million at an $8 billion valuation, per Bloomberg, and fal said the two rounds come to $1.65 billion combined... Investors have now put more than $1.9 billion into the company.

key_facts.fact: Fal passed $800 million in annualized revenue earlier this year, according to a person familiar with the matter cited by Bloomberg.
key_facts.excerpt: Annualized revenue at fal passed $800 million earlier this year, a person familiar with the matter told Bloomberg.

key_facts.fact: CEO Burkay Gur said demand outran compute: the company had to rate-limit customers over the summer. The money goes to compute and hiring beyond its 185 employees.
key_facts.excerpt: "We hit a point in summer where we were not able to serve our customers and had to rate-limit them," he said... The company will spend the money on computing power and on hiring beyond its current 185 employees.

key_facts.fact: Rival Fireworks AI closed $1.5 billion at a $17.5 billion valuation in July, while gross margins across inference companies remain thin because compute is expensive to buy or lease.
key_facts.excerpt: rival inference provider Fireworks AI Inc., which closed $1.5 billion in funding at a $17.5 billion valuation in July. Several people familiar with the finances of inference companies told TechCrunch that gross margins across the sector remain thin because compute is expensive to buy or lease.

key_facts.fact: Bessemer names Adobe, Canva, Shopify, World Labs and Amazon among the companies that have moved production volume to Fal.
key_facts.excerpt: Many of the world's largest companies, like Adobe, Canva, Shopify, World Labs, Amazon, and more, have moved production volume to fal.

stories.headline: OpenAI to buy Pierre Computer, moving Codex into code storage and challenging GitHub

key_facts.fact: OpenAI will acquire Pierre Computer, a developer tools startup whose technology is already embedded in Codex, the company told Axios on November 4. Financial terms were not disclosed.
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI will acquire Pierre Computer, a developer tools startup whose technology is already embedded in Codex, the company told Axios exclusively... Financial terms were not disclosed.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI plans to integrate Pierre's Code Storage into Codex; Pierre's open-source projects will remain open source.
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI plans to integrate Pierre's Code Storage function into Codex, where Pierre's technology is already used... Pierre's open-source projects will remain open-source.

key_facts.fact: Axios frames the deal as OpenAI joining companies challenging Microsoft's GitHub as AI agents take on more coding work.
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI is joining a slew of companies challenging Microsoft's GitHub as AI agents take on more coding work.

key_facts.fact: Code Storage is a distributed storage system built on Git with APIs designed for machines, supporting repositories as large as 32TB; Pierre names Lovable, Bolt and Amp among its users.
key_facts.excerpt: a distributed storage system built on Git, with API ergonomics designed for machines... Pierre names Lovable, Poke, Anything, Bolt, Amp and Parahelp among the service's users... repositories as large as 32TB

key_facts.fact: The deal follows OpenAI's November 2 post on Pando, its own Git backend for its monorepo, which it says cut median push latency by nearly 80% after agent workloads strained earlier systems.
key_facts.excerpt: In a November 2, 2026, engineering post, OpenAI described Pando... switching to Pando reduced median push latency by nearly 80%

stories.headline: Anthropic open-sources FlashProve, which cryptographically proves which model produced a response

key_facts.fact: Anthropic announced FlashProve on X on November 3 (its research post is dated November 2): a system that lets developers verify whether a given response came from a given AI model, substantially more efficiently than prior open-source methods.
key_facts.excerpt: FlashProve allows developers to verify whether a given response came from a given AI model. It's substantially more efficient than prior open-source methods for doing so.

key_facts.fact: The problem it targets: users cannot currently check that a response came from the claimed model rather than one swapped in by a routing service to save costs, or from an attacker tampering with the token stream.
key_facts.excerpt: as opposed to one secretly substituted in by a routing service for cost reasons, or even by an attacker who has tampered with the token stream.

key_facts.fact: On Llama 4 Maverick, a 400B-parameter model, a single H100 GPU generates proofs at about 110 tokens per second with proofs of about 19 MB per 1,024-token request, using about 70-95 times the GPU time of running the model on vLLM.
key_facts.excerpt: a single H100 GPU generates proofs at around 110 tokens/second, with a proof size of ~19 MB per 1,024-token request... This is ~70-95x the GPU time of running the model itself on vLLM

key_facts.fact: Anthropic says Claude produced the zkSNARK (a type of cryptographic proof) improvements and wrote the protocol specification; because its decisions can be hard to evaluate, the top-level security claims are stated in the Lean formal verification language for auditing.
key_facts.excerpt: Claude has produced improvements on zkSNARKs for inference... Claude is good at optimization, but often makes decisions that are hard to evaluate... providing top-level auditable statements in Lean

key_facts.fact: Applications Anthropic cites include letting safety evaluators confirm the model they test is the one served to customers, and contributing to a toolkit for verifying compliance with AI pacing requirements.
key_facts.excerpt: independent evaluators who test AI models before and after release need to know that the model they are evaluating is the model being served... could contribute to a toolkit for verifying compliance with AI pacing requirements.

key_facts.fact: The code, Lean proofs and documentation are released under Apache 2.0, and Anthropic describes the work as intermediate progress rather than a finished agenda; collaborators come from EPFL, MIT, StarkWare and Succinct.
key_facts.excerpt: We release our code, Lean proofs, and documentation under the Apache 2.0 license. This research post is meant to share intermediate progress, and not a completed research agenda.
